It's True
2013-07-29T00:00:48+06:00 | The Daily Star
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/its-true-71

The hurdy-gurdy is a stringed musical instrument that produces sound by a crank-turned rosined wheel rubbing against the strings. The wheel functions much like a violin bow, and single notes played on the instrument sound similar to a violin. Melodies are played on a keyboard that presses tangents against one or more of the strings to change their pitch. The hurdy-gurdy is generally thought to have originated from fiddles in either Western Europe or the Middle East some time prior to the eleventh century A.D. The most popular use of the instrument is found in Swiss folk-metal band Eluveitie.
